inspection_outcome: Three established issues: one core nonlinear range defect and two local false statements
summary: Fixed mean-zero bifurcation range fails; exact fixed projection repairs this step. C4 parameter differentiability and the general full-rotation-group multiplicity also require local correction.
limitations: No counterexample to the principal existence theorem is claimed.
The local repairs do not certify the entire repaired proof.
Findings bind the online-first publisher file; older arXiv v2 not fully compared.
Supplement/code and correction searches were bounded.

problems.title: Physical boundary mean does not define the fixed mean-zero nonlinear range

labels: Section 6 definition and inversion of S

problems.claim: S_rho(w)=w-F(rho,w) maps fixed mean-zero C^{2,alpha} to fixed mean-zero C^{1,alpha}.
problems.assumptions: Actual radial domain pullback; N=2, G=D5, h=cos(5theta)/sqrt(pi); max(rho0,1/sigma)<rho<1/lambda_bar_2; sufficiently small nonzero epsilon; actual PDE solution of Proposition 4.1.
problems.check_method: Exact weighted mean identity and first-order shape derivative; second-order nonzero fixed mean, with analytic positive quadratic form.
problems.decisive_evidence: J_eh=1+(N-1)epsilon h+O(epsilon^2); F_eh=-c_rho epsilon H_rho h+o(epsilon). Hence integral F_eh=(N-1)c_rho epsilon^2 integral h H_rho h+o(epsilon^2)>0. Positivity follows from rho sigma>1, Lemma 2.3 and (5.2)-(5.3).
problems.result: An actual admissible small perturbation leaves the asserted fixed mean-zero codomain. The inverse-function construction is not defined as printed.
problems.counterevidence: At w=0 the linearization preserves zero mean, so linear checks alone do not detect the nonlinear defect. No contradiction to the principal existence theorem was obtained.
problems.impact: Core Banach-space inverse and ensuing bifurcation formulation require correction; Major despite a short repair.

correction.statement: Replace F by P0 q_w=P0 F, with P0 the fixed sphere mean-zero projection, and S by w-P0F.
correction.verification: The corrected range is fixed mean-zero; its zeros are exactly constant normal derivative; D(P0F)=-c_rho H_rho is unchanged on the mean-zero space.
correction.status: Local repair analytically verified; entire repaired theorem not independently certified.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Current primary read publisher pp6,8-9,16-17,19,23. Fixed sphere mean-zero spaces and radial identification are explicit; Eq4.4 subtracts physical-boundary mean, not fixed-sphere mean. Actual image of p17 inspected.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Exact identity integral(F J)=0 with J=1+(N-1)epsilon h+O(epsilon^2) and F=-c epsilon Hh+o(epsilon) yields fixed integral(F)=(N-1)c epsilon^2 integral(hHh)+o(epsilon^2). For allowed D5 h=cos5theta/sqrt(pi), choose rho near the allowed upper endpoint so rho sigma>1; Q inequality from Lemma2.3 and Eq5.3 makes this coefficient strictly positive. Thus S at the actual PDE solution leaves the fixed codomain.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: F itself initially maps to the unrestricted space, but the Section6 inversion explicitly uses fixed mean zero and fails. Linearization at w=0 preserves the fixed mean and does not cure the second-order range error. This is a central bifurcation-construction defect, not a counterexample to existence.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: P0 q=P0 F has exactly the same zeros and linearization; local repair confirmed, full corrected bifurcation theorem not certified.

problems.title: The radial solution family is not C1 with values in C4
problems.claim: U: (0,lambda_bar_2^{-1}) -> C4(Bbar), rho -> u_rho, is C1.
problems.assumptions: N=3; rho*=1/(16pi^2) in (0,1/(4pi^2)); unique nodal radius and negative annulus as in Proposition 3.1.
problems.check_method: Explicit outer linear radial ODE and contradiction from the second derivative jump in the parameter-differentiated PDE.
problems.decisive_evidence: p_rho=1-pi sqrt(rho), p*=3/4, p'_rho*=-2pi^2. If v=d_rho u exists in C4, v(p*)=2pi^2 a!=0 for a=u'(p*)<0. In -Delta u-rho Delta v=(1-3(u+)^2)v the left side is C2 but the right second radial derivative jumps by -6 a^2 v(p*)!=0.
problems.result: C4-valued parameter differentiability fails at this admissible parameter.
problems.counterevidence: Individual spatial C^{4,alpha} regularity remains compatible; the radial nondegeneracy proof was checked and does not depend on the false C4 parameter claim.
problems.impact: Overstated parameter regularity; lower regularity suffices for the Section 4 construction, with no separate demonstrated failure of the main theorem.

correction.verification: The semilinear map to C^{0,alpha}_r is C1; Proposition 3.2(a) and Schauder theory give an invertible radial derivative; IFT plus uniqueness glues the local branches.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Publisher pp9,12-13 explicitly gives unique radial node and C1 map into C4 for every0<rho<lambda2bar^-1.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For N3 the negative-annulus equation for r u is y''+rho^-1 y=0 and consecutive zeros give p=1-pi sqrt(rho). At rho*=1/(16pi^2), p=3/4 and p'=-2pi^2. A hypothetical C4 parameter derivative v has v(p)=2pi^2 u'(p) nonzero. The twice-radial derivative of (1-3(u+)^2)v jumps by-6u'(p)^2 v(p), whereas -Delta u-rho Delta v is C2. This contradicts C4-valued differentiability.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: Individual spatial C4,alpha and radial nondegeneracy are not contradicted; Section4 only needs lower parameter regularity. Minor reflects this supporting overstatement's bounded dependency.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: C1 dependence into C2,alpha follows from the actual nondegenerate radial linearization and the C1 semilinear map; no stronger regularity inferred.

problems.title: General invariant multiplicity for the full 600-cell rotation group lacks a square
problems.claim: The displayed single-factor character average a_i equals dim H_i(S3)^G for all even i.
problems.assumptions: G is the full 7200-element rotation group specified in the article, G=(2I x 2I)/diag{+/-1}; i=60 is an allowed even degree.
problems.check_method: Left/right SU(2) harmonic decomposition and exact character evaluation; primary reference equation (2.47) checked visually.
problems.decisive_evidence: H_i complexified=V_i tensor V_i*, so full G invariants have dimension (dim V_i^{2I})^2=a_i^2. At i=60, a_i=(61+20+12+12+15)/60=2, actual multiplicity=4.
problems.result: The claimed general dimension gives 2 instead of 4 at degree 60.
problems.counterevidence: Degrees 2,4,6,8,10 give 0 and degree12 gives1; squaring preserves all values used to establish (G).
problems.impact: Local general formula incorrect; the N=4 low-degree application survives.

correction.statement: m(i)=a_i^2 for even i and zero for odd i, squaring the whole coefficient and bracket.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Publisher pp26-27 specify the full7200-element rotation group and all even degrees. Current primary actually viewed Nelson-Widom p12 Eq2.47 with the square.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: H_i(S3;C)=V_i tensor V_i* and the group=(2I x2I)/diag+-1 give multiplicity a_i^2. At i60 every nonidentity character ratio is1, so a60=2 while dimension=4. Odd invariants vanish; low degrees used for(G) remain0 or1 after squaring.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: Only the unnecessary general high-degree formula fails; the actual N4 symmetry application and first invariant degree12 remain valid.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Square the entire character average for even i, including1/60; exact representation-theoretic repair.

clarifications.text: The negative-part test is u^-; PDF text extraction loses the superscript. Actual images resolve this and no defect is alleged.
